## Catchment overview {#sec-overview}

Sagelva is a small catchment (109 km²) draining to Nitelva in the western part of Lillestrøm kommune. Land cover is dominated by forest (71 %), but with significant urban (16 %) and agricultural (6 %) areas. See @fig-sagelva and @tbl-sagelva-land-cover. The catchment is classified as *leirpåvirket* (clay-influenced) under the Water Framework Directive and about 14 % of the catchment is underlain by marine sediments and clays (@tbl-leir-totp-bounds). 

![Maps of the Sagelva catchment. Left: Land cover based NIBIO's AR50 dataset. Right: Point source discharges from industry and municipal wastewater plants (≥50 p.e.).](./plots/sagelva.png){#fig-sagelva width=800 fig-align="center"}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sagelva-land-cover
#| tbl-cap: "Land cover proportions for Sagelva based on NIBIO's AR50 dataset."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd

catch = "Sagelva"

# Read land cover data
df = pd.read_excel(r"./data/catchment_land_cover.xlsx")
df = df.set_index("klasse")

# Create total row
total = df.sum(numeric_only=True)
total.name = "Totalt"
df = pd.concat([df, total.to_frame().T])

# Convert to MultiIndex
new_cols = []
for col in df.columns:
    catchment, statistic = col.rsplit("_", 1)
    if statistic == "km2":
        statistic = "km²"
    elif statistic == "pct":
        statistic = "%"
    new_cols.append((catchment, statistic))
df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(new_cols, names=["Nedbørfelt", "AR50 klasse"])

# Select catchment
df = df[[catch]]

# Format
km2_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c[1] == "km²"]
pct_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c[1] == "%"]
for col in pct_cols:
    df[col] = df[col].round().astype(int)
fmt = {c: "{:.1f}" for c in km2_cols}

# Style
df.style.format(fmt).set_table_styles(
    [
        {"selector": "th.col_heading", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
        {"selector": "th.col_heading.level0", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
        {"selector": "th.col_heading.level1", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
    ]
).map(lambda _: "font-weight: bold;", subset=pd.IndexSlice[["Totalt"], :])
```

There are no major industrial discharges within the Sagelva catchment and the only municipal wastewater plant with design capacity ≥50 p.e. is Mariholtet sportsstue, but this reports low discharges of nutrients (@tbl-sagelva-pt-sources).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-sagelva-pt-sources
#| tbl-cap: "Industrial and municipal wastewater discharges within the Sagelva catchment."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd

cat_list = ["Sagelva"]

# Read point source data
df = pd.read_excel(r"./data/point_discharges.xlsx", sheet_name="point_locs").query(
    "name in @cat_list"
)

# Convert to tonnes
pars = ["TOTN", "TOTP", "TOC", "SS"]
for par in pars:
    df[f"{par} (tonn)"] = df[f"{par}_kg"] / 1000

# Tidy
rename_dict = {
    "site_name": "Navn",
    "sector": "Sektor",
    "type": "Type",
}
df = df.rename(columns=rename_dict)
val_cols = [f"{par} (tonn)" for par in pars]
text_cols = list(rename_dict.values())
df = df[text_cols + val_cols]

# Format and style
fmt = {c: "{:.2f}" for c in val_cols}
df.style.format(fmt).hide(axis="index").set_properties(
    subset=text_cols, **{"text-align": "center"}
).set_table_styles(
    [{"selector": "th.col_heading", "props": [("text-align", "center")]}]
)
```

## Monitoring data {#sec-sagelva-monitoring}

The best monitoring data for Sagelva comes from Vannmiljø stations `002-46599` (Sagelva ved Skjetten bro, F3) and `002-63540` (Fjellhammarelva, F10), both of which are located within waterbody `002-3899-R` (Fjellhamarelva - Sagelva) in the lower part of the catchment (blue triangles on @fig-sagelva). Skjetten bro is the downstream-most station with the longest monitoring record, beginning in 1995. 

@fig-sagelva-ann-concs shows trends in mean annual concentrations estimated from the combined dataset for waterbody `002-3899-R`. Concentrations of SS and TOTP have remained broadly stable over the past 30 years, but there has been a significant decline in TOTN concentrations (by about -8 μg-N/l/year) and a significant increase in TOC concentrations (about +0.1 mg-C/l/year). 

In terms of water quality status, concentrations of TOTN have improved from the middle of the *moderate* class in 2010 to close to the boundary between *moderate* and *good* in 2023-25. If this trend continues, waterbody `002-3899-R` will likely achieve Good Ecological Status (GES) for TOTN in the coming years. For TOTP, concentrations are broadly stable at around 40 μg-P/l. This corresponds to the boundary between *moderate* and *good* status for a catchment of this type with around 20 % marine clay cover. For TOC, there appears to be a step-change increase in concentrations between 2012 and 2013. This may be due to changes in water sampling or analysis protocols, although according to Vannmiljø the reporting lab has not changed.

![Trends in annual mean concentrations for waterbody `002-3899-R` (Fjellhamarelva - Sagelva). Solid red lines show statistically significant linear trends ($p ≤ 0.05$); dashed red lines indicate weak evidence of a linear trend ($0.05 < p ≤ 0.10$); and dashed black lines indicate no statistically significant trend ($p > 0.10$). Background colours show thresholds for water quality status defined under the Water Framework Directive and taken from Vann-Nett, where available (*bad*, *poor*, *moderate*, *good* and *high*).](./plots/concs/ann_trends_waterbodies_002-3899-R.png){#fig-sagelva-ann-concs width=800 fig-align="center"}

## Source apportionment {#sec-sagelva-sources}

@fig-teotil3-sagelva shows nutrient fluxes estimated from observed data (black lines) together with source-apportioned fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 (stacked bars). TEOTIL3's simulations for TOTN are broadly in agreement with the monitoring data, and results for TOC are also reasonable. For TOTP and - especially - SS, annual fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 are higher than the estimates based on monitoring data. It is possible that TEOTIL3 is overestimating losses of particulate material (SS and TPP) in this catchment. However, it is also likely that particulate fluxes (TPP and SS) estimated from infrequent sampling data underestimate the true nutrient load (see @sec-ann-loads).

Given the uncertainties in both monitoring and modelling, it is reasonable to suggest that nutrient fluxes from Sagelva are approximately:

 * 40 to 60 tonnes/year for TOTN
 * 2 to 4 tonnes/year for TOTP
 * 300 to 600 tonnes/year for TOC
 * 1000 to 2000 tonnes/year for SS

![Annual nutrient fluxes for waterbody `002-3899-R` (Fjellhamarelva - Sagelva). Black lines show fluxes estimated from monitoring data; stacked bars show source-apportioned fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3.](./plots/modelled/mod_vs_obs_default_Sagelva_waterbody_002-3899-R.png){#fig-teotil3-sagelva width=800 fig-align="center"}

@fig-sagelva-src-app shows the mean percentage contribution from each source to annual fluxes for the period from 2020 to 2024. According to TEOTIL3, agriculture is the dominant source of TOTN, TOTP and SS, but there are significant contributions from urban runoff in the lower part of the catchment, which is densely populated. TOC fluxes are dominated by background inputs from forest areas in the south of the catchment (@fig-sagelva). The contribution from wastewater discharges in this catchment is small: about 5 % for TOTP and less than 3 % for TOTN, TOC and SS. There are no large municipal wastewater plants in this catchment. The wastewater contribution to TOTP simulated by TEOTIL3 comes from spredt (1 %) and wastewater overflows (4 %). It is important to note, however, that the overflow dataset provided by Lillestrøm kommune only includes discharges within the kommune boundary, which only covers the northern-most part of the Sagelva catchment (@fig-catchments). The true contribution from wastewater overflows would be greater if discharges from neighbouring kommuner, such as Lørenskog, were included.

![Mean source-apportionment for waterbody `002-3899-R` (Fjellhamarelva - Sagelva) based on TEOTIL3 simulations from 2020 to 2024. For clarity, labels are omitted for sources contributing less than 3 %.](./plots/modelled/src_app_default_Sagelva_waterbody_002-3899-R.png){#fig-sagelva-src-app width=800 fig-align="center"}

## Load reductions and scenarios {#sec-sagelva-avlast}

During the decade from 2015 to 2024, the median annual flow volume from Sagelva (station `002-46599`) was 46 Mm³/year. Taking the maximum concentrations for GES of 775 μg/l for N and 40 μg/l for P, the maximum annual load for "good" status is approximately 40 tonnes for TOTN and 2 tonnes for TOTP. These values are at the lower limit of nutrient loads measured in recent years (@fig-teotil3-sagelva). Combining the same GES thresholds with the annual flow time series from NVE, we calculate an avlastningsbehov for each year from 2015 to 2024, using both observed nutrient loads (black lines on @fig-teotil3-sagelva) and loads modelled using TEOTIL3 (stacked bars on @fig-teotil3-sagelva).

@fig-sagelva-avlast shows the distribution of annual avlastningsbehovene for the period from 2015 to 2024. Since TOTN fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 are slightly lower than fluxes calculated from monitoring data (@fig-teotil3-sagelva), the median avlastningsbehov from TEOTIL3 (8 %) is lower than that based on monitoring data (19 %). The distributions based on both modelled and observed data are broad, suggesting that in some some years reductions of more than 25 % would be required to maintain "good" status. However, overall, reduction targets of 10 to 20 % seem reasonable for TOTN.

For TOTP, the fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 are generally higher than estimates based on monitoring data. Monitored fluxes are usually around 2 tonnes per year, but occasionally up to ~4 tonnes per year. Since 2 tonnes per year is close to the maximum for GES, the median avlastningsbehov based on observed data is small (3 %), although in some years it is a high as 15 %. TEOTIL results are typically less variable, with simulated TOTP fluxes usually around 3 tonnes per year. This gives a much higher median avlastningsbehov of 40 % (@tbl-scen_summary-sagelva).

![Distributions of annual avlastningsbehovene (in percent) for the ten year period from 2015 to 2024 based on observed fluxes (red curves) and fluxes simulated by TEOTIL3 (blue curves). Vertical dashed lines show the median avlastningsbehov based on each dataset i.e. the load reduction that would have achieved GES in roughly half of the ten year period.](./plots/modelled/avlast_Sagelva_waterbody_002-3899-R.png){#fig-sagelva-avlast width=800 fig-align="center"}

@fig-sagelva-scens shows the load reductions achieved for the Sagelva catchment by two scenarios modelled by [Wallhead *et al.* (2026)](https://www.miljodirektoratet.no/publikasjoner/2026/april-2026/modellering-av-oslofjorden-scenarier-med-redusert-menneskelig-belastning-for-a-oppna-god-okologisk-tilstand/). Since there are no significant discharges from municipal wastewater plants to Sagelva, all reductions in this catchment are achieved by agricultural measures. The required TOTN reductions for GES of 10 to 20 % cannot be achieved by scenario A, but could plausibly be achieved by scenario B, which includes more measures targeting agricultural losses of N.

For TOTP, scenarios A and B both comfortably exceed the 3 % reduction target estimated from the monitoring data. Scenario B achieves TOTP reductions of 37 %, which is approximately equal to the avlastningsbehov based on TEOTIL3 simulations. A summary of the avlastningsbehovene for GES in Sagelva and the reductions achieved by scenarios A and B is shown in @tbl-scen_summary-sagelva.

![Load reductions achieved in the Sagelva catchment by scenarios A and B of [Wallhead *et al.* (2026)](https://www.miljodirektoratet.no/publikasjoner/2026/april-2026/modellering-av-oslofjorden-scenarier-med-redusert-menneskelig-belastning-for-a-oppna-god-okologisk-tilstand/). Black vertical lines on the plots for TOTN and TOTP show the median avlastningsbehov for GES estimated using observed data (@fig-sagelva-avlast).](./plots/modelled/oslomod_scens_Sagelva.png){#fig-sagelva-scens width=800 fig-align="center"}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scen_summary-sagelva
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of avlastningsbehov and scenario results for Sagelva."
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd

catch = "Sagelva"

# Read site data
xl_path = r"./data/scenario_summary.xlsx"
df = pd.read_excel(xl_path).query("`Nedbørfelt` == @catch")

wfd_col_dict = {
    "High": "#5893A9",
    "Good": "#6FB22C",
    "Moderate": "#FFF6A6",
    "Poor": "#F6A800",
    "Bad": "#E63D5C",
}


def color_wfd(val):
    color = wfd_col_dict.get(val)
    if not color:
        return ""

    text_color = "white" if val in ["Poor", "Bad"] else "black"
    return f"background-color: {color}; color: black;"


# Format
txt_cols = ["Nedbørfelt", "Vannforekomst ID", "Parameter", "Vann-Nett tilstand"]
num_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in txt_cols]
df[num_cols] = df[num_cols].round().astype("Int64")

# Style
(
    df.style.hide(axis="index")
    .format(na_rep="")
    .map(color_wfd, subset=["Vann-Nett tilstand"])
    .set_table_styles(
        [{"selector": "th.col_heading", "props": [("text-align", "center")]}]
    )
    .set_properties(subset=txt_cols, **{"text-align": "center"})
    .set_properties(subset=num_cols, **{"text-align": "right"})
)
```
